Academic Requirements.content:
To be eligible for admission, candidates shall comply with the General Regulations and the Regulations for Taught Postgraduate Curricula; and shall hold:
- a **Bachelor’s degree in the urban or related fields** of this University; or
- a qualification of equivalent standard of this University or another university or comparable institution accepted for this purpose;
- preferably a **professional qualification in the urban or related fields**; and
- satisfy the examiners in a **qualifying examination if required**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Applicants with qualifications from a university or comparable institution outside Hong Kong where the language of teaching or examination is not English are required (unless exceptionally exempted) to obtain:
- **a score of 80 or above (internet-based test) in the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL)**; or
- **a minimum overall band of 6.0 with no subtest lower than 5.5 in the International English Language Testing System (IELTS)**.
Required documents include **TOEFL / IELTS transcript (if appropriate)**.

Program Overview.content:
The Master of Science in Urban Analytics (MSc(Urban Analytics)) is offered as a one-year full-time programme. The evolving technological basis of cities is reshaping our urban life and allowing us to understand, plan, manage and optimise cities in completely new ways. The MSc(Urban Analytics) programme is designed to train and upskill students and professionals able to apply novel urban science and analytics in planning and managing the development of cities. Aiming to bridge the disciplines of social science, urban planning and design and data science, the programme provides a balance between analytical and practical skills on the one hand, and on the other, domain knowledge and urban theory from social, economic, behavioural, environmental and management sciences.
**Programme aims**
- Equip students and urban professionals with cutting-edge analytics and modelling skills
- Enable good understanding of urban sciences underlying smart city development techniques
- Support urban policy makers and urban planning/design/surveying practitioners with urban analytics
**Professional Accreditation**
MUA has received “specialist” accreditation from the Royal Town Planning Institute (RTPI). Graduates could become members of RTPI under the [Associate Route](https://www.rtpi.org.uk/membership/about-rtpi-membership/apply/associate/). They can become RTPI Associate Members after 2 years of planning experience and then become RTPI [Chartered Member](https://www.rtpi.org.uk/membership/about-rtpi-membership/apply/chartered-town-planner/) after another 2 years of planning experience via [A-APC](https://www.rtpi.org.uk/membership/assessment-of-professional-competence/associate-apc/).
**Careers of Graduates**
The majority of MUA graduates are working in planning and design institute/company/organizations in HK and Mainland China. Another group of students find urban analytics/data scientist jobs in world leading finance and internet companies.
**Main Teaching Staff**
Yeh, Anthony G.O.; Ma, Jun; Yang, Tianren; Zhang, Xiaohu; Zhao, Zhan; Zhou, Yulun.

Curriculum.content:
MSc(Urban Analytics) requires **69 credits within the 1-year full-time study**. The curriculum of the programme consists of seven urban analytics courses (6 credits each), two urban theory courses (6 credits each; two from an approved list of courses), and a dissertation/capstone project (15 credits).
**Urban analytics courses (Compulsory)**
- Programming and Foundations in Urban Data Analysis
- Geographic Information System (GIS) for Urban and Regional Planning Development
- Urban Big Data Analytics
- Artificial Intelligence for Future Cities
- Spatial Mobilities Analytics
- Spatial Planning Analytics
- Science of Cities
**Urban theory courses (Choose Two)**
- Urban Development Theories
- Planning Practice, Law and Ethics in Hong Kong
- Public Transport Systems
- Transport Policy and Planning
- Transport Economics
- Transport Network Analysis and Modelling
- Housing, Planning and Sustainability
- Globalization and Urban and Regional Development in China
- Planning Future Cities and Regions
- International Planning Policy and Practice
- Housing Economics
- Transitional Cities: Urban and Housing Development
- Design, Survey and Modelling for Urban Health
- Principles of Healthy Cities
- Values of Urban Design: Urban, Social, Environmental Economics
- Morphologies and Urban Design Theories
\* The course list may vary at the time of selection.
**Dissertation/ capstone project**
- Dissertation OR
- Smart Planning and Design Studio

Cost of Attendance.content:
For HKU postgraduate students, estimated living-expense budget items for 2026/27 include:
- Books and supplies (excluding personal computers & accessories): around **HK$11,440-HK$55,600 p.a.**
- University's residential halls & colleges lodging fees: **HK$27,000-HK$92,000 p.a.**
- Hall miscellaneous charges: **HK$2,000-HK$3,000 p.a.**; these include students' association membership fees, compulsory high table fees, room and/or smartcard deposits, etc., excluding air-conditioning charge which varies with individual lifestyle and seasons (approximately **HK$200 per month in summer**).
- Compulsory hall meal charges: **HK$9,000-HK$12,000 p.a.** (not all meals are covered).
- CEDARS-administered non-hall housing lodging fees: **HK$20,000 p.a.-HK$120,000 p.a.**
- Food, groceries, transportation and others: around **HK$6,100 per month up** depending on lifestyle and grocery shopping around campus.
- Other personal expenses: phone services, entertainment, overseas travel, insurance and medical expenses, etc.
**Estimated Cost of Living Outside Campus by Month (Per Person) for reference only**: all figures are estimates for 2026/27 and subject to inflation and lifestyle.
| Item | HKD |
| --- | --- |
| Rent for Off-Campus Accommodation (depending on the size, location and type of accommodation) | $8,000-20,000 |
| Utilities | $1,000 |
| Food | $6,000 |
| Local Transportation | $500 |
| Personal Miscellaneous | $1,500 |
| Total | $17,000-29,000 |
Other expenses when renting outside campus include agent commission, typically **50% of one month's rent** if renting through an agent; deposit, usually **2 months' rent**; and stamp duty, around **HK$300** for a HK$10,000/month rental. Typically, students would expect spending an average of **HK$25-HK$65 per meal** on campus. Transportation reference fares include Sassoon Road to Main Campus **HK$2-7** by University shuttle bus or **HK$5.1-14.5** by bus/minibus; Main Campus to Central **HK$5.9-9.4**; and Main Campus to Causeway Bay/Mongkok **HK$5.9-20**. For non-local students, expenses for the first month can amount to **HK$10,000 or more** on top of tuition fees, including rental charges, household items and textbooks.

Financial Aid.content:
MUA Entrance Award: Up to two awards shall be awarded annually to full-time postgraduate students who are permanent residents in Hong Kong and who have been admitted to the MUA programme, on the basis of academic merit, publication of undergraduate dissertation, academic-related activities and achievements.
**International Scholarship for Taught Postgraduate Studies in the Department of Urban Planning and Design** **(subject to approval by the University)**
- Each self-funded taught postgraduate programme shall award a maximum of one Scholarship per year, to be determined by a Selection Committee.
- Entrance scholarship to deserving international students (i.e. excluding Hong Kong and Mainland China) who have been offered admission into the programme based on:
1. academic merit at the time of admission (e.g. academic/professional achievements);
2. Performance at admission interview; and
3. Personal statement.
- The waiver of each scholarship shall cover the composition fee of the respective taught postgraduate programme, resulting in a waiver of the composition fee for the awardee.
- Recipients of the Scholarship shall be expected to actively participate in departmental and programme promotional activities.

Multiple Applications.content: Yes, it is possible for you to apply to multiple programmes at HKU. You can apply under different usernames on the application system and pay the application fee (**HK$600**) for each programme that you wish to apply to. You can only enrol in one programme, even if you receive offers from other programmes.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: No, you should submit your application again for the next year admission. You may contact our academic programme officers if in doubt. Please [click here](https://www.arch.hku.hk/media/upload/Table-2-Q12-Q13-Contact-Information-for-TPG-program-20161229.pdf) to download the contact information.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you have not completed your undergraduate study at the time of application, you are required to provide your latest official transcript of your current study and other available documents to the Faculty for admission panel’s consideration. If you receive a **conditional offer of admission** subsequently, you are required to resubmit the finalized official transcript in due course for vetting purpose.
Applicants who receive a **Conditional Offer letter** should forward visa application documents to the Hong Kong Immigration Department via CEDARS (for overseas students) or China Affairs Office (for mainland students), and are advised to apply as soon as possible because visa completion takes around **8-10 weeks**.
If an applicant receives a Conditional Offer and pays the deposit for securing the place, then receives the Firm Offer later, the applicant must settle the balance of the first installment of the composition fee and the caution money (**HKD 350**) by the deadline stated in the Firm Offer letter.
